blocks.heading: Product types and purpose
blocks.text: Consumer products are bought for personal or household use; producer goods are bought by businesses to make other goods or services; they include capital goods such as machinery and equipment, and materials or components used up in production. Durable goods are used repeatedly over time, while non-durable goods are used up more quickly. Services provide an activity or benefit rather than ownership of a new physical good. Classify using purpose and characteristics: the same item can be a household consumer durable or business equipment depending on who buys it and why. The categories can overlap because they answer different questions.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A household buys a freezer for its food; a meal business buys a freezer to support production. The first is a consumer durable, the second business equipment or a capital good. Both are physical durable items; buying purpose changes the consumer/producer distinction.
